headline: What EXPERTS EXPECT for Gold and Silver Prices in June 2026: Key Events to Watch
snippet: Analysts surveyed by CBS News see gold trading between $4,400–$4,700 through June as the Fed's June 16–17 meeting looms, with June 5 payrolls and June 10–11 CPI/PPI prints as key volatility catalysts. Multiple experts flagged silver's industrial demand profile — driven by solar and EVs — as the more compelling setup heading into H2 2026.

headline: GOLD REBOUNDS to $4,580 Off Two-Month Lows as PCE Inflation Soothes Fed Fears
snippet: Gold recovered from $4,380 two-month lows — its weakest since late March — to trade back above $4,500 after April PCE inflation data matched consensus, easing concerns about an accelerated Fed tightening cycle. The metal posted a second straight session gain Friday to $4,580 on reports of a potential 60-day US-Iran ceasefire extension.

headline: China Importing 790+ TONNES of Silver in Early 2026: SWOT Says Demand Still Accelerating
snippet: VanEck's weekly Gold SWOT analysis highlights that China imported over 790 tonnes of silver in early 2026, driven by its rapidly expanding solar manufacturing capacity, while combined global visible inventories across COMEX, LBMA, and Shanghai continue a multi-year decline. The note flags silver's current price near $76/oz — well below its $116 January peak — as a potentially asymmetric entry relative to an accelerating industrial demand base.

headline: SILVER ENTERS SIXTH DEFICIT YEAR as Solar Tech Upgrades Drain 1 Billion oz From Vaults
snippet: The global silver market is running its sixth consecutive annual supply deficit — estimated at 46 to 150+ million ounces short in 2026 — as manufacturers migrate to next-generation TOPCon and SHJ solar cell architectures that require 50–100% more silver per gigawatt than legacy PERC cells. Supply cannot easily respond: 70% of silver is mined as a byproduct and combined COMEX, LBMA, and Shanghai visible stocks have lost nearly one billion ounces since 2021.

headline: GDX LAGGING 25 POINTS Behind Bullion — Analysts Say Miner Catch-Up Trade Is Building
snippet: While spot gold surged 60% in 2025, GDX gained only 35–40% and junior miner ETF GDXJ lagged further — a valuation gap analysts argue is unsustainable given that producers are now generating record cash flows at current metal prices. With multiple Wall Street desks forecasting $5,000–$6,000+ gold for 2026, junior explorers with near-term drill catalysts are seen as the highest-asymmetry exposure in the sector.

headline: COPPER STAGES COMEBACK Near $6.40/lb: Second Monthly Advance as AI Build-Out Drives Demand
snippet: Copper futures tracked toward a second consecutive monthly advance at end of May, underpinned by AI-driven data-center construction that JPMorgan estimates could consume 475,000 tonnes of copper in 2026 alone. A projected 330,000-tonne refined-market shortfall and production disruptions in Chile maintain the structural bull case, with Freeport-McMoRan, Southern Copper, and Teck among analyst favorites.

headline: ENERGY STORAGE BOOM Lifts Beaten-Down Lithium Demand Outlook After Two Years of Pain
snippet: A surge in grid-scale battery energy storage deployments is reviving lithium's demand outlook after two years of price depression, with Chinese lithium carbonate prices surging 78% since mid-December 2025 on Chinese supply concerns and stronger demand. Broker Guotai Junan projects energy storage will account for 31% of global lithium demand in 2026, up from 23% in 2025, with storage now outpacing EV batteries as the primary growth driver.

headline: URANIUM AT $84.50: Spot Retreats From $101 Peak as Market Debates Shortage vs. Surplus
snippet: Uranium spot prices settled near $84.50/lb in late May as speculative momentum behind January's $101 high fully unwound, yet long-term contract prices hold at $90/lb and utility 'uncovered requirements' are at record levels. Kazatomprom projects a 21-million-pound supply deficit by 2030, and Denison Mines' Final Investment Decision to build the Phoenix in-situ recovery mine in Saskatchewan marks the first new permitted uranium mine to break ground in over a decade.

headline: AUSTRALIA BOOTS Six China-Linked Investors From Rare Earth Developer Northern Minerals
snippet: Australian Treasurer Jim Chalmers issued formal divestment orders requiring six China-linked entities to sell their combined ~18% stake in Northern Minerals (ASX: NTU), developer of the Browns Range Heavy Rare Earths Project in Western Australia — one of very few non-Chinese sources of dysprosium and terbium critical for EV and defense magnets. Shares fell over 8% on the May 17 announcement as the government cited national security concerns under the Foreign Acquisitions and Takeovers Act.

headline: CHINA'S RARE EARTH EXPORT PAUSE Nears November Expiry — Supply Chains Still Dependent
snippet: The 12-month suspension of China's expanded rare earth export controls is set to expire November 10, 2026, with analysts warning that Western supply chains have made limited progress in reducing dependence on Chinese rare earth processing. Controls already in force require case-by-case export licences for seven critical heavy rare earth elements — dysprosium, terbium, lutetium, and others — essential for next-generation magnets and defense systems.
